subject: Next Steps & Decision Map: Inference Platform evaluation for Acme
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Next Steps & Decision Map: Inference Platform evaluation for Acme

Hi Lara —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Pain points (as discussed):
- Latency variability on peak traffic (user-facing search/chat): 250–600ms spikes impacting conversion.
- High token cost from current hosted provider and unpredictable burst charges.
- Security/compliance: need VPC controls, audit logs, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Current stack:
- Backend: Node + Go microservices, deployed in GCP us-central1.
- Models: mix of Open weights served via a third-party hosted endpoint; team also runs limited on-prem experiments.
- Observability: Datadog + internal tracing; no token-level cost telemetry today.

Success criteria for pilot (you said):
- 20–30% reduction in per-token cost or equivalent reduction in monthly spend at current volumes.
- P95 inference latency below 200ms for the 512-token tail.
- Ability to route sensitive workloads to a VPC-backed private deployment and produce audit logs.

Procurement & decision map (initial framing):
- Decision stakeholders we should expect: Lara (Product), Michael Ortiz (Procurement), and one Security reviewer (TBD).
- Timeline: procurement kickoff in late Apr / early May; target pilot contract signed by end of May.
- Initial commercial guardrail: you indicated an expected committed spend band of ~$8k–$20k/month as a starting point for pilot budgeting.
- Eval criteria: technical PO, procurement T&C review, and a 30-day pilot with telemetry handoff.

Next concrete steps I propose:
1) I attached a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft to capture owners and dates.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra and security team (30–45m).
3) I’ll loop Michael into procurement thread and share preliminary commercial guardrails so procurement has context.

Can you confirm: (a) the procurement contact (is Michael the right person to include?), (b) the right security reviewer name, and (c) whether the budget band above matches your expectations for the pilot?

I attached the MAP and SLA summary for quick reference.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0132

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf (stub), SLA-Overview.pdf (stub)

Thanks Rafael — this is great and accurate.

Confirmations:
- Procurement: Michael Ortiz (michael.ortiz@acmecorp.com) is the right person; I’ll intro him in a separate note.
- Security reviewer: attaching name is pending but initial contact is Priya Natarajan (Cloud Security Lead) — I’ll make the intro.
- Budget band: $8k–$20k/month aligns with our pilot sizing; we may flex on term for a proven SLA.

One more detail: our compliance team requires a short data residency statement for pilot telemetry — can you confirm where telemetry will be stored for a VPC pilot? If it’s within GCP us-central1 that should be fine.

Avail for tech deep-dive: Wed 21 Apr 11:00–12:00 PT or Thu 22 Apr 09:00–10:00 PT.

Lara

Acme Corp

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Fwd: Next Steps & Decision Map: Inference Platform evaluation for Acme

Michael — looping you in as Lara suggested. Rafael from Redwood here.

Short context: Acme is evaluating a pilot for inference platform to reduce cost and stabilize latency; key stakeholders: Lara (Product), Priya (Security), Michael (Procurement).

I attached the MAP draft and SLA doc. Quick answers:
- Telemetry for a VPC pilot: platform control plane remains in Redwood control plane (encrypted at rest in GCP us-central1) but sensitive payloads and logs tied to customer workloads can be directed to your VPC and stored in your controlled buckets. We will provide SOC2 artifacts and an architecture diagram in the tech deep-dive.

Proposed times for tech deep-dive per Lara’s availability: Wed 2026-04-21 11:00 PT or Thu 2026-04-22 09:00 PT — we’ll hold 45m. Please confirm which works for you and if procurement wants a separate seat.

Next: if Michael confirms procurement acceptance of the initial guardrail, we’ll send a short SOW draft to help procurement evaluate commercial terms.

Thanks — Rafael
